references.text: Moses met God on the mountain in the burning bush, and he is one of the two men who appear together with Jesus on the Mount of Transfiguration.
Moses' face shone after speaking with God on Mount Sinai, which forms a parallel to Jesus' transfiguration on the mountain.
Moses prophesied about a coming prophet like himself, and his presence on the Mount of Transfiguration confirms Jesus as the fulfillment of this prophecy.
Elijah is a central prophetic figure in the Old Testament, and his presence together with Moses points to how the Law and the Prophets testify about Jesus.
Elijah met God on Mount Horeb (Sinai), which parallels the scene on the Mount of Transfiguration where he again stands in God's presence.
Malachi mentions both the law of Moses and the prophet Elijah who is to come, and both these figures appear with Jesus on the Mount of Transfiguration.
Matthew's parallel account of the transfiguration on the mountain where Moses and Elijah appear and speak with Jesus.
Mark's parallel account of the transfiguration on the mountain where Elijah and Moses appear and speak with Jesus.
The next verse elaborates on what Moses and Elijah spoke with Jesus about, namely his departure (exodus) which he was to accomplish in Jerusalem.
Philip testifies that Jesus is the one whom Moses in the Law and the Prophets wrote about, which is confirmed by the presence of Moses and Elijah on the Mount of Transfiguration.

The two witnesses in Revelation have traits reminiscent of both Moses (plagues over the waters) and Elijah (fire from his mouth, shutting up the sky), the two who appeared with Jesus on the Mount of Transfiguration.
